model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for several language model variants. The x-axis represents the number of iterations (#Iteration), displayed on a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 140,000, with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents Loss, also on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2.

Six lines are shown in the plot. The "Vanilla" line, in light blue/lavender, starts at approximately 3.4 at iteration 0 and decreases steeply in the early iterations before gradually leveling off, reaching approximately 2.62 by iteration 140,000; this line remains consistently above most other lines throughout training. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" line, in a brighter cyan/blue, follows a similar trajectory to the Vanilla line, starting near 3.4 and declining to approximately 2.60–2.62 by the end, tracking closely with or very slightly below the Vanilla line. The "SepLLM (n=64)" line, in orange, starts near 3.4 and decreases more aggressively, reaching approximately 2.52–2.53 by iteration 140,000, placing it noticeably below the Vanilla and StrmLLM lines. The "SepLLM (n=64, H)" line, in dark green/olive, follows a very similar path to SepLLM (n=64), ending at approximately 2.51–2.53. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" line, in red, also tracks closely with the other SepLLM variants, ending near 2.50–2.52. The "SepLLM (n=128)" line, in dark purple/indigo, follows a nearly identical trajectory to the other SepLLM variants, ending at approximately 2.50–2.52. All lines exhibit a characteristic rapid decrease in the first ~20,000 iterations followed by a more gradual decline. The four SepLLM variants cluster tightly together in the lower portion of the plot, while the Vanilla and StrmLLM lines cluster together at higher loss values throughout training.
